title: Hachimi Mambo: Career Survival Agent
bullets: One Skill: career-survival
JiuwenSwarm 0.2.4b3, single-agent mode
Five questions, in order

title: 1. How we thought while designing the Skill
bullets: An early exit is scored from the state at exit: survival is a constraint
Seven ordered priorities; a higher rule wins, with stated exceptions
Every number is our own safety margin, labelled as policy
48 months: survive, climb, then protect and build wealth

title: 2. What the logs showed, and what we changed
bullets: 26 games; 9 eliminations, 7 at the first level
Optional costs + weak review -> cash margin
Story choice cost a promotion -> protect reviews
Late reaction to warnings -> risk gauge, incident count
Risk-cutting after weak reviews -> performance first
61M -> 38M tokens a game: one Skill, no code
This version: 6 games, all 48 months, mean about 65

title: 3. Scripts and reference files
bullets: None in the final Skill
An earlier Python ledger was called inconsistently and bloated the context
Decisions only compare a few small numbers
One short document: one place to look

title: 4. How general and robust the Skill is
bullets: Public statistics, grades, listed effects and tone only
No event names, story wording or event order
Stalled actions judged by the change actually observed
Margins on published scales, not fitted to development games

title: 5. Agents and agent Skills
bullets: The model is capable but inconsistent
A Skill gives a stable way of working and carries lessons forward
Short and ordered beats long and complete
Limits: no forced compliance, no hidden rules, no removal of randomness

title: Thank you
bullets: Hachimi Mambo
Career Survival Agent
